subject.title: [Security] Unsafe deserialization of incoming WebSocket commands in Gateway

question: Does a schema-valid inbound Gateway frame containing prototype-sensitive keys reach any concrete merge or assignment sink that changes a target object's prototype on current main?
rationale: The claimed parsing primitive is not itself exploitable, but only a security owner should close the protected report or route a confirmed sink into a private advisory after reviewing the full dispatcher and plugin-handler boundary.

options.title: Close after sink audit
options.body: Confirm no schema-valid frame reaches a prototype-mutating sink, document the negative reproduction, and close the public report as not reproducible.

options.title: Move to private advisory
options.body: If a concrete sink is demonstrated, preserve sensitive reproduction details in a private GHSA and develop a narrowly scoped fix and regression test there.

recommendation.title: Close after sink audit
recommendation.body: Confirm no schema-valid frame reaches a prototype-mutating sink, document the negative reproduction, and close the public report as not reproducible.

likelyOwner.reason: The history shows broad ownership across Gateway protocol changes and repository security advisory publication.
